about: Stored-manifest seal cases (SPEC §4, §7; ADR-0066; #573, #901). Each case is a stored pair: 'manifest' is the bytes of manifest.json as the UTF-8 string they spell ('manifest_hex', lower-case hex, in its place when they are not UTF-8) and 'seal' the content of manifest.seal (null = the member is missing). A reader takes the bytes, never a string decoded from them. Every reader reaches every verdict: the Rust reader (tessera-core tests/seal_cases.rs), the reference reader (reference_reader/run.py) and tessera-wasm (seal_verdict, natively and in Node), so they agree by construction. Verdicts, in ADR-0066 rule 4's order (a case with two faults has the verdict of the first): 'refused' = not read: no seal (the pre-ADR-0066 alpha layout, rule 10) or a seal that is not exactly 'blake3:' + 64 lower-case hex; not I-JSON (a duplicate key, NaN, a lone surrogate, nesting deeper than 127, a number beyond a double's range or whose value is an integer beyond ±(2^53−1) in any spelling, #886); not its own RFC 8785 JCS form (key order, whitespace, an escape or a number spelling JCS doesn't write, such as #901's sealed 64.0, a pretty layout); a 'manifest_hash' key in band; then, past the seal, a value in a form SPEC §5 doesn't declare (a record as an array, a block kind as an object, metadata: [], study: 5, a block kind or name outside its grammar, a block class other than 'derived'), an unsupported major tessera_version, a block listed twice or without a digest, a chunk index (kind chunk_index or a spec with 'indexes', whatever its name or class) whose 'indexes' is not another listed block (SPEC §5d, #720). 'tampered' = the seal is not blake3 of the bytes, or id or content_hash doesn't match (a missing content_hash too, or one computed over a derived block: content_hash is over the primary blocks only, a block ref's 'class' is absent or exactly 'derived', ADR-0028 §4, #720). 'ok' = verifies. Families per corpus product: as-stored, newer-field-resealed (verifies, names the field), field-spliced (old seal), T4-T7 under the old seal and S7/S8 sealed by the attacker (the #897 spike's respellings), S5b (an exact double beyond 2^53, its own JCS form, refused by I-JSON), alpha-layout, seal-in-band-resealed. newer_fields = what the Rust view reports as not interpreted, each path rendered unambiguously (SPEC §4). Generated by reference_reader/make_seal_cases.py from corpus/files.
